Subject: Lena Hart — score variance + reconciliation checklist

Team —

Thanks for interviewing Lena yesterday. Quick heads-up: Ben and Mina submitted scores that diverge by >2 points on 'system design (scale)' and 'ownership/impact'. We need a short reconciliation so we can close the loop with recruiting and decide on calibration.

Can each of you do two things by EOD Monday:
- Drop a short justification (1–2 bullets) in the scorecard doc explaining the high/low marks
- Add any follow-up clarifying question you want on the doc (I can send to Lena if we decide to re-run a quick 30m)

I've attached the resume and a fresh scorecard template. Link to scorecard: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB_example_scorecard_doc

If you think a 15m sync would be faster, flag your availability and I'll coordinate.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lena Hart — score variance + reconciliation checklist

Thanks Marissa — quick notes from me (I'll paste into the doc as well):
- System design (scale) — 7/10: Lena's approach favored single-region, strongly-consistent reads with sharding at the application layer. In an ML-serving context we prefer read-latency first and multi-region failover; I downgraded because I didn't see explicit caching/async replication choices.
- Ownership/impact — 6/10: She described owning a team but it was small (3 engineers) and most impact examples were intern-level features. Strong execution but less cross-org influence.

If you want an alignment sync, I'm free Mon 11:30–12:15 or Tue 09:00–09:30 PT.

-Ben
Ben Carter | Staff SWE (Hiring Interviewer)
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Lena Hart — score variance + reconciliation checklist

Adding my perspective — will add bullets to the sheet too but copying the key points here:
- System design (scale) — 8/10: I rated higher because she had a clear partitioning approach and mentioned a KV cache + TTL strategy; she was explicit about cache invalidation trade-offs. The multi-region bit was lighter but I thought her latency-first justification acceptable.
- Ownership/impact — 8/10: Lena's story about shipping a customer-facing inference pipeline that led to a 12% latency reduction (measured) felt substantive — cross-functional coordination included.

Ben — can you point to which piece of the interview made you think the replication/cross-region plan was absent? I'm trying to reconcile the 7 vs 8.

-Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lena Hart — score variance + reconciliation checklist

Appreciate the quicks. To keep this lightweight, two options:
1) Consolidate comments in the scorecard doc and I'll summarize for recruiting (preferred)
2) 15m async huddle — Wed 09:00 PT (I'll send invite if both of you can)

Ben — Karthik's question is fair. Ben, if you can paste the exact quote or time window from the interview where the replication plan felt missing, that would help. Karthik: similarly paste the line you referenced about TTL/cache. I'll stitch both into a 2-line reconciliation note.

Mina — I didn't see your scores yet. Can you drop them into the sheet? If you don't have time, mark NA but add whether you'd prefer 'move forward' or 'no hire'.

Marissa
